```{r}
#| include: false

source("R/efile_helpers.R")

rel     <- efile_release("v3_1")
rel_pf  <- efile_current("990PF")
cc      <- efile_concordance()
counts  <- efile_nonempty(efile_counts(rel))
meta    <- efile_table_meta(counts$table, cc, rel$form)
cov     <- efile_coverage(efile_counts(rel), efile_counts(rel_pf))
fil     <- efile_filings(counts)
yrs     <- range(counts$year)
```

The NCCS 990 Efile database turns the XML returns that nonprofits file electronically with the IRS into `r length(unique(counts$table))` relational tables, one or more for each Part of Form 990, Form 990-EZ, and their Schedules. Every table is published for each tax year in two formats, **CSV** and **Parquet**.

| | |
|:--|:--|
| **Release** | `r efile_label(rel)` (published `r rel$published`) |
| **Returns** | Form 990 and Form 990-EZ, with schedules |
| **Tax years** | `r yrs[1]`&ndash;`r yrs[2]` (`r yrs[2]` is a partial year) |
| **Tables** | `r length(unique(counts$table))` tables, `r fmt_n(nrow(counts))` table-year files |
| **Filings** | `r fmt_n(sum(fil$rows_tot))` returns |
| **Labels** | concordance990 `r cc$version` |
| **Private foundations** | Form 990-PF returns are a separate database: [`r efile_label(rel_pf)` catalog](`r rel_pf$page`) |

## About this release {#about}

### Data sources and processing

IRS 990 e-file returns are published by the IRS as XML documents. NCCS builds this database from the XML files indexed by the [Giving Tuesday 990 Data Commons](https://www.givingtuesday.org/data-commons/990-data-infrastructure/), supplemented with returns the IRS e-file index lists but the Data Commons index never picked up (see the release notes below).

Each XML element (xpath) is assigned to a research variable and a table by the **Master Concordance** ([concordance990](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/concordance990/)), and the tables are built with the [ef2](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/ef2/) package. A table holds one Part of a form or schedule: either one row per filing (**1:1**), or several rows per filing for repeating groups such as officers, grants, or program service accomplishments (**1:M**).

Efile data are organized by **tax year**, the closest approximation to the calendar year in which the nonprofit's activities took place. The tax year (`TAX_YEAR`) is the year in which the fiscal year begins (`TAX_PERIOD_BEGIN_DATE`). Returns are due five months after the fiscal year ends, and the IRS releases them in monthly batches, so the most recent tax year is always incomplete and keeps growing for two to three years.

Every table carries the keys needed to join tables to each other and to the BMF: `OBJECTID` (`OID-` followed by 18 digits, one per filing), `EIN2`, and `TAX_YEAR`. One-to-many tables add `TABLE_ID` (`TID-NNN-NNN-NNN`, one per row). Every row also carries `URL`, a link to the source XML return: open it to confirm whether a value is missing from the return or was not captured by the concordance.

## Coverage {#coverage}

Before tax year 2021, electronic filing was required only for the largest nonprofits (more than $10 million in assets) and for private foundations. Other organizations adopted it gradually. Beginning with tax year 2021 (calendar year 2022), e-filing is mandatory for almost all tax-exempt organizations, so recent waves cover nearly the full population of 990 and 990-EZ filers. For earlier years, the larger an organization is, the more likely it filed electronically; sample weights can be built by comparing efilers with the BMF or the NCCS Core files.

While most parts of Form 990 and its schedules are public, [some sensitive information is redacted by the IRS or nonprofits to protect the privacy of donors](https://www.adlercolvin.com/blog/2015/06/08/exempt-organizations-can-redact-donor-identifying-information-from-irs-form-990-schedule-b-before-public-disclosure/).

## Table and file names {#file-names}

Table names follow the pattern **FF-PPP-TTT-NAME**, and each file appends the tax year: `F9-P07-T01-COMPENSATION-2023.parquet`.

- **FF** is the form: `F9` = Form 990, `SA` = Schedule A, `SB` = Schedule B, and so on.
- **PPP** is the part: `P01` = Part I, `P02` = Part II, and so on. `P00` is the heading and `P99` holds lines outside any part or from earlier versions of the form.
- **TTT** is the table: `T00` holds the one-to-one fields of the part, and `T01`, `T02`, ... are its one-to-many tables.

Tables whose names end in `-EZ` hold lines that appear only on Form 990-EZ. All other tables pool the matching lines from the 990 and the 990-EZ.

Each table-year is published as **CSV** (readable anywhere) and **Parquet** (smaller and much faster in R with `arrow` or `duckdb`; panel990 reads Parquet by default). Both files hold the same rows and columns. Table-years with no filings are omitted from the listings below.
